questions.question_text: When watching the hazard perception clips, when should you click?
options: As soon as you see a potential hazard
Only when the hazard actually happens
At regular intervals regardless of the road
questions.explanation: The test measures how quickly you identify a hazard developing so you can respond safely.

questions.question_text: How many clips are usually shown in the hazard perception part of the test?
questions.explanation: The test typically consists of 14 video clips, with at least one hazard in each, and one clip containing two hazards.

questions.question_text: What happens if you click your mouse too many times during a hazard perception clip?
options: You are disqualified from the test
You score zero for that specific clip
You get an extra chance to re-watch the clip
You have to wait for the next clip
questions.explanation: Excessive clicking or 'pattern clicking' is treated as cheating, and the system will award no points for that clip.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum score you can get for a single hazard?
questions.explanation: The earlier you identify the hazard and click, the higher your score, with 5 points being the maximum per hazard.

questions.question_text: What should you do if you think you missed a hazard during a clip?
options: Ask the examiner to play it again
Continue to scan the road and watch for the next one
Click on everything just in case
questions.explanation: You cannot go back and watch clips again, so focus on the remainder of the clip and the following ones.
